about: Open Problem Garden, MathOverflow, Mathematics Stack Exchange and arXiv-abstract problems in the catalogue that are already settled elsewhere, so scripts/build_data.mjs stops listing them as open (formalized ones become known results, unformalized ones are dropped). MathOverflow and Math.SE: status checked through the Stack Exchange API on 2026-11-28; a question counts as settled when it has an accepted answer, an upvoted answer (score >= 3, or citing a published resolution) that settles it, or when it was closed as a duplicate of a settled question; partial, hedged or conditional answers were not counted. Open Problem Garden and arXiv: settled only with an explicit public source (paper, OPG comment citing one, or follow-up paper). Problems proved in this repository (proofs/<id>.lean) are excluded.

opg-a-game-on-an-n-x-n-grid.reason: Solved: the first player wins the square achievement game if and only if n >= 5 (Reid, with Lean-formalized proofs).

opg-are-critical-k-forests-tight.reason: Disproved: Gebauer, Gundert, Moser and Okamoto give a saturated (critical) 3-forest that is not tight, resolving Strausz's problem.

opg-bene-conjecture-graph-theoretic-form.reason: Disproved: for every N >= 2 there is a simple N-regular ordered two-stage graph L_N with F(L_N) = 2 and R(L_N) >= N, refuting R(L) <= 2F(L) as stated on OPG (the companion partition-stabilizer form is already recorded as known).

opg-book-thickness-of-subdivisions.reason: Disproved: Dujmovic, Eppstein, Hickingbotham, Morin and Wood construct graphs of queue-number at most 4 and unbounded stack-number, resolving the Blankenship-Oporowski problem (Combinatorica 2022).

opg-chromatic-number-of-common-graphs.reason: Answered negatively: Kral, Volec and Wei construct common graphs of arbitrarily large chromatic number.

opg-complete-bipartite-subgraphs-of-perf.reason: Proved by Scott, Seymour and Spirkl (Pure pairs V, Combinatorica 2023): every perfect graph has a pure pair of sizes at least eps n^(1-c), i.e. a large complete bipartite subgraph in G or its complement.

opg-cores-of-strongly-regular-graphs.reason: Proved by Roberson: every endomorphism of a primitive strongly regular graph is an automorphism or a colouring, so its core is itself or complete (confirming Cameron-Kazanidis).

opg-covering-systems-with-big-moduli.reason: Answered negatively: Hough proved that the least modulus of a covering system with distinct moduli is at most 10^18 (Annals 2015).

opg-erdos-posa-property-for-long-directe.reason: Proved as a consequence of the directed grid theorem: Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer show that directed cycles of length at least l have the (vertex) Erdos-Posa property for every l (STOC 2015).

opg-every-prism-over-a-3-connected-plana.reason: Disproved: Spacapan constructed a 3-connected planar graph whose prism is not Hamiltonian (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 2021).

opg-extremal-problem-on-the-number-of-tr.reason: Proved by Csikvari and Lin: among trees on m vertices the path has the fewest and the star the most endomorphisms.

opg-finite-satisfiability-of-positive-ho.reason: Solved by Bova and Mogavero (LICS 2017): via finite quasi-Herbrand models, entailment and finite entailment for positive Horn (quantified conjunctive) sentences coincide, answering Chen-Madelaine-Martin.

opg-goldbergs-conjecture.reason: Proved by Chen, Jing and Zang (Proof of the Goldberg-Seymour conjecture, J. Comb. Optim. 50 (2025)).

opg-grunbaums-conjecture.reason: Disproved: Kochol constructed snarks with polyhedral embeddings in every orientable surface of genus at least 5, whose duals are triangulations that are not 3-edge-colourable (as the OPG comments record).

opg-highly-arc-transitive-two-ended-digr.reason: Disproved: DeVos, Mohar and Samal construct two-ended highly arc-transitive digraphs whose tiles are not disjoint unions of complete bipartite graphs.

opg-laplacian-degrees-of-a-graph.reason: Proved by Brouwer and Haemers: the j-th largest Laplacian eigenvalue of a connected graph is at least d_j - j + 2 (Linear Algebra Appl. 429 (2008) 2131-2135).

opg-number-of-cliques-in-minor-closed-cl.reason: Answered positively by Lee and Oum: graphs with no K_t subdivision (hence no K_t minor) have at most 2^(50t) n cliques; Fox and Wei later found the sharp constant.

opg-ptas-for-feedback-arc-set-in-tournam.reason: Answered: Kenyon-Mathieu and Schudy gave a PTAS for (weighted) feedback arc set in tournaments (STOC 2007).

opg-rank-vs-genus.reason: Answered: Tao Li constructed closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds whose rank is smaller than their Heegaard genus, with arbitrarily large discrepancy (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2013).

opg-real-roots-of-the-flow-polynomial.reason: False: there are flow polynomials with real roots above 4 (Royle 2009), and Jacobsen and Salas found graphs whose flow roots exceed 5.

opg-seymours-self-minor-conjecture.reason: Disproved as stated (every infinite graph): Oporowski gave an uncountable graph that is not a proper minor of itself (J. Graph Theory 14 (1990) 521-524); the countable case is a different, still open question.

opg-shuffle-exchange-conjecture.reason: Disproved as stated (for all k, n >= 2): d(k,3) = 6 > 2n-1 = 5 for every k >= 3; the binary case k = 2 is not decided by this.

opg-shuffle-exchange-conjecture-graph-th.reason: Disproved as stated: for the directed shuffle-exchange network d(k,3) = 6 for every k >= 3, not 2n-1 = 5; the binary case k = 2 is not decided by this.

opg-snevilys-conjecture.reason: Proved by Arsovski (Israel J. Math. 182 (2011), 505-508); Harcos, Karolyi and Kos give a shortened proof.

opg-subgroup-formed-by-elements-of-order.reason: Frobenius' conjecture was proved by Iiyori and Yamaki using the classification of finite simple groups (Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 25 (1991)), as the OPG comments cite.

opg-textbf-convex-fair-partitions-of-con.reason: Proved by Akopyan, Avvakumov and Karasev: every planar convex body can be partitioned into m convex pieces of equal area and perimeter for every m >= 2.

opg-universal-highly-arc-transitive-digr.reason: Answered positively: DeVos, Mohar and Samal construct a locally finite highly arc-transitive digraph with universal reachability relation.

opg-what-is-the-largest-graph-of-positiv.reason: Answered by Ghidelli: every planar PCC graph has at most 208 vertices, and 208 is attained (Nicholson-Sneddon).
